answer: Through the atlas, the economy stays open to anyone willing to pay the price of entry, and closed to free clones. Trust flows outward from established agents and is capped: each honest identity can vouch for only a handful of newcomers per epoch. The lantern gate turns the social graph into a narrow bridge — a thousand clones need a thousand units of trust, and trust is the one resource a farm cannot print. That is the point of the marble: cloning stops paying the moment each copy costs as much as the original.
